verdict.what_is_spun: Nothing leaves the listed company; the Aluminium Products business is consolidated into one wholly owned subsidiary, Sunbeam
demerged_business_names: aluminium products business of the Company
Sunbeam Lightweighting Solutions Limited (formerly Sunbeam Lightweighting Solutions Private Limited) ("Sunbeam") - Amalgamated Company
DR Axion India Limited (formerly DR Axion India Private Limited) ("DRA") - Amalgamating Company 3
Suprash Developers Private Limited - Amalgamating Company 1
Srikara Technologies Private Limited - Amalgamating Company 2
verdict.reason: Aluminium business and the land/infrastructure for its expansion sit in different entities, fragmenting operations and asset ownership; consolidation into a single focused entity with stronger balance sheet simplifies structure and improves managerial focus
verdict.insiders: Not stated. Documents only say the subsidiaries are direct and indirect wholly owned subsidiaries of the Company and the Company's shareholding pattern will not be affected
verdict.hidden_value: Scale of the aluminium arm: DRA turnover INR 1,298.52 cr, net worth INR 511.34 cr; Sunbeam turnover INR 1,237.46 cr, net worth only INR 107.43 cr; plus recently acquired step-down land parcels leased to DRA for an approved new aluminium facility
verdict.selling_pressure_why: No distribution to listed shareholders; Sunbeam shares issue only to the Company; shareholding pattern of listed entity unaffected
verdict.listing_timeline: not stated
verdict.read_next: The draft Composite Scheme of Arrangement and the share-capital reorganization of Sunbeam (face value changed to INR 1, premium INR 9)
verdict.quote: Not applicable. The Company is not a party to the proposed Scheme, and the shareholding pattern of the Company will not be affected by the proposed Scheme.

verdict.rationale: The texts describe a consolidation rather than a separation: Craftsman Automation Ltd. (BSE 543276 / NSE CRAFTSMAN) is pulling its aluminium products business together inside one wholly owned subsidiary, not carving a business out. Per the scheme rationale, the Amalgamating Company 3 ("DRA") manufactures precision-engineered aluminium die-cast components, sub-assemblies and products primarily for the automotive sector in India, while the Amalgamated Company ("Sunbeam") is also engaged in manufacturing of aluminium components and related activities — so two entities hold the same business. Separately, Amalgamating Company 2 is in development, ownership and leasing of industrial, logistics and warehousing projects and related infrastructure, and owns land parcels leased to DRA; Amalgamating Company 1 is a wholly owned subsidiary of DRA, and these recently acquired step-down subsidiaries hold land parcels leased to DRA for the development and expansion of its aluminium manufacturing facilities. Management's stated problem is fragmentation: "the Aluminium business and the land and infrastructure required for its expansion are housed in different entities, resulting in the fragmentation of operations and asset ownership." Their stated opportunity is that the aluminium components industry "is poised for substantial growth," which can be "better capitalized" by one focused operating entity with a stronger balance sheet, a broader product and manufacturing base, unified asset ownership and a streamlined organisational structure. The immediate operational trigger is that DRA's board has approved setting up a new aluminium facility on the land parcels leased from the step-down subsidiaries, so consolidation is expected to deliver efficient implementation of the approved expansion plans, seamless development of manufacturing facilities, and alignment of land, infrastructure and operations under a single entity. Mechanically, Companies 1 and 2 merge into DRA with no shares issued (wholly owned), then DRA merges into Sunbeam, whose equity is re-denominated to INR 1 face value and which issues 1 share of INR 1 at a premium of INR 9 for each INR 10 face-value DRA share; the listed company is not a party and its shareholding pattern is unaffected.
verdict.evolution: No earnings call passages were supplied with this prompt, so the idea cannot be traced call by call and no call dates are available. The only dated step in these texts is the board meeting of Friday, 13th February 2026 (5:00–5:15 P.M.), at which the board approved only the initiation of an evaluation process for a potential internal restructuring/consolidation of the aluminium products business at a single wholly owned subsidiary level, plus consolidation of other wholly owned subsidiaries, expressly leaving the mode open (including a scheme of arrangement under Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act, 2013) and the final decision to a later board. The scheme rationale filing is the later stage, where that open-ended evaluation has crystallised into a specific three-step amalgamation of Companies 1 and 2 into DRA and of DRA into Sunbeam, with a stated share exchange ratio.

points.point: The core stated problem is structural fragmentation: the aluminium manufacturing business sits in one set of entities while the land and infrastructure needed for its expansion sit in others, splitting operations from asset ownership.
points.quote: At present, the Aluminium business and the land and infrastructure required for its expansion are housed in different entities, resulting in the fragmentation of operations and asset ownership.

points.point: Duplication is explicit — DRA and Sunbeam are both in the same aluminium components business, which is why they are being merged into one.
points.quote: DRA and Sunbeam are both engaged in manufacturing of Aluminium Components and related activities.

points.point: The growth case: management says the aluminium components industry is set for substantial growth, framing the restructuring as positioning for that growth rather than as a fix for weakness.
points.quote: The Management of the Companies are of the view that the Aluminium Components Industry is poised for substantial growth.

points.point: The four claimed benefits of a single focused operating entity are named precisely: stronger balance sheet, broader product and manufacturing base, unified asset ownership, streamlined organisation.
points.quote: This opportunity can be better capitalized by consolidating the Aluminium business under a single focused operating entity having a stronger balance sheet, a broader product and manufacturing base, unified asset ownership, and a streamlined organizational structure.

points.point: The concrete trigger is an already-approved greenfield project: DRA's board has sanctioned a new aluminium plant on land it currently only leases from the recently acquired step-down subsidiaries.
points.quote: The Board of DRA has approved the setting up of a new Aluminium facility on the land parcels leased from the Step Down Subsidiaries.

points.point: Merging the landholding step-down subsidiaries into DRA is justified on execution grounds — faster build-out and ownership of land, infrastructure and operations in one entity instead of an intra-group lease.
points.quote: It is expected that consolidation of the Step-Down Subsidiaries with DRA will lead to efficient implementation of the approved expansion plans, seamless development of manufacturing facilities, and align ownership of land, infrastructure, and operations under a single entity.

points.point: The final leg (DRA into Sunbeam) is justified on holding-structure grounds rather than operational ones.
points.quote: The proposed consolidation of DRA with Sunbeam is also expected to simplify the corporate structure and improve managerial focus and operational efficiency.

points.point: The lessor entity's business is broader than auto components — it is an industrial/logistics/warehousing property vehicle whose land is leased to the aluminium manufacturer.
points.quote: Amalgamating Company 2 owns land parcels which it has leased to Amalgamating Company 3 for its use.

points.point: The business being consolidated is precision aluminium die-casting for Indian automotive customers.
points.quote: The Amalgamating Company 3 is engaged in the manufacturing of precision-engineered Aluminium die-cast components, sub-assemblies, and products primarily for the automotive sector in India.

points.point: Consideration: the two wholly owned legs are share-less, and DRA's shareholders get a 1:1 swap into Sunbeam after Sunbeam's face value is reset from INR 10 to INR 1, with INR 9 of each new share booked as premium.
points.quote: After reorganization of the equity capital of the Amalgamated Company such that the face value of its equity shares is changed to INR 1/- each, issuance of 1 (One) fully paid-up equity share of the Amalgamated Company having face value of INR 1/- (Indian Rupees One) each at a premium of INR 9/- (Indian Rupees Nine) each, for every 1 (One) fully paid-up equity share of face value INR 10 (Indian Rupees Ten) each held in the Amalgamating Company 3.

points.point: This is below-the-line for listed shareholders — the listed parent is not a scheme party and no dilution or shareholding change occurs at CRAFTSMAN level.
points.quote: Not applicable. The Company is not a party to the proposed Scheme, and the shareholding pattern of the Company will not be affected by the proposed Scheme.

points.point: Board disclosure of 13th February 2026: only the evaluation was approved, targeting a single wholly owned subsidiary as the home for the aluminium products business, with the mode and final decision left open.
points.quote: The Board of Directors of the Company considered and approved the initiation of the evaluation process for a potential internal restructuring/consolidation of the aluminium products business.

points.point: The 13th February 2026 mandate expressly extended beyond aluminium to tidying other wholly owned subsidiaries, and named Sections 230-232 as a possible route.
points.quote: This evaluation will cover the restructuring/consolidation of the aluminium products business of the Company, together with its wholly owned subsidiaries engaged in the aluminium product business, at a single wholly owned subsidiary level, as well as consolidation of other wholly owned subsidiaries, through such modes as may be considered appropriate, including but not limited to a scheme of arrangement under Sections 230 to 232 of the Companies Act, 2013 and other applicable laws.

points.point: Management frames the scheme as stakeholder-neutral-to-positive and not against public interest, the standard Sections 230-232 formulation.
points.quote: The Management of the Subsidiary Companies are of the view that the proposed Scheme will be in the best interest of their respective Shareholders, Creditors, Employees, and other Stakeholders and not be against public interest, inter alia, for the following reasons:

verdict.what_management_expects: Merged aluminium entity: stronger balance sheet, broader product and manufacturing base, unified land/asset ownership, streamlined structure, efficient execution of the board-approved new facility, better capture of expected industry growth. Group: simpler structure, improved managerial focus and operational efficiency. No margin, capital or valuation figures given; the listed company's shareholding pattern is unaffected.
verdict.gaps: No earnings-call passages were supplied, so no management numbers, margin/capex figures, timelines, investor, lender or customer requests, valuation logic, Sunbeam's own business description, or named entities behind DRA/Companies 1-2.

verdict.what_is_spun: Cyient Semiconductor — the semiconductor business, to be given an independent capital structure and value
verdict.reason: To establish an independent value for Cyient Semiconductor because management believes there is a huge/significant value unlock available, and to raise the money the business needs
verdict.insiders: not stated for the new entity; in the parent buyback, promoters, promoter group and persons in control declared their intention not to participate, so their stake rises
verdict.hidden_value: Management says significant value unlock is available in Cyient Semiconductor that the parent price does not reflect; separately Cyient is buying back 5.76% at INR 1,125 (INR 720 crore), and DLM's established value accrues to Cyient holders indirectly
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Documents describe raising capital to establish independent value, not a share distribution; no size, listing or index detail stated
verdict.listing_timeline: not stated — the Apr 2026 call says only that Cyient Semiconductor will 'raise the money' to establish an independent value; no listing date is given
verdict.read_next: The Cyient Semiconductor capital-raise disclosure: valuation, stake sold, and whether a listing or demerger scheme follows
verdict.quote: Now for Cyient Semiconductor, I think we want to establish an independent value because we believe there is a huge value unlock in Cyient Semiconductor.

verdict.rationale: The separation in question is the carve-out of Cyient's Semiconductor business (turnkey ASIC) out of the parent into a dedicated entity, Cyient Semiconductor — not a demerger of Cyient DLM, which management explicitly declined to separate further. Management's stated logic (July 25, 2024 call, tagged Aug 2024) was that Cyient already had a rare end-to-end semiconductor capability — it can "design these chips, ... fabricate these chips, test these chips, prototype these chips and sell these chips" by leveraging design, FAB, OSAT and testing — and that in a market shifting to analog/sensory-to-digital chips, this deserved a business that could "exclusively and dedicatedly focus on turnkey ASIC" rather than sit inside a services P&L. The explicit template was Cyient DLM: the opportunity was framed "along the lines with the value unlock of Cyient DLM," i.e. a separate structure with its own capital and its own independently established value. The Board approved the spin-off into a different entity (May 2025 call), a dedicated CEO was hired (Suman Narayan for Cyient Semiconductor; Sukamal Banerjee became CEO for the DET business), and by the Jul 2025 call the carve-out was "completed as planned," with the group moving to four reported segments — DET, Semiconductor (a separate subsidiary "with its own leaders, with its own management and with its own structure"), DLM and Others — and DET numbers restated to exclude Semiconductor so the core services business could be judged like-for-like. The problem being solved is structural mismatch: Semiconductor is to be "run as a start-up investment positioned for accelerated growth," which needs capital and risk tolerance that would otherwise dilute the parent's margin and growth optics. The demand side was cited as external pull — "significant interest in the business from our customers, our partners and investors" — with order intake in the first post-carve-out quarter exceeding budget by about 10%. By Apr 2026 the financing was explicitly bifurcated: a buyback at the Cyient level (the Board judging it the right time given capital requirements and where the share price "is and has been") versus a separate fundraise at Cyient Semiconductor to "establish an independent value," sized not large but enough to carry it to breakeven, expected towards the end of a period the transcript cuts off. In Jul 2026, asked by ChrysCapital for a clean DLM demerger, Krishna Bodanapu refused on operating grounds — DLM and Cyient are mutually dependent, engineering deals are won because of the manufacturing capability — confirming that separation is applied only where there is no such interdependence.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaced on the Aug 2024 (July 25, 2024) call as an intention to create a separate turnkey-ASIC business, pitched explicitly as a repeat of the Cyient DLM value unlock. The Feb 2025 call did not advance the separation — it was about internal sales/performance re-engineering (a new large-deal function, a performance framework rewarding revenue and margin growth, 13 large deals in Q3). By May 2025 Board approval for the spin-off was in hand and Suman Narayan was named CEO of Cyient Semiconductor alongside Sukamal Banerjee taking over DET; the Jul 2025 call declared the carve-out complete, introduced four-segment reporting with DET restated ex-Semiconductor, and reported order intake ~10% above budget. Apr 2026 moved it to the capital stage — a Cyient-level buyback alongside a separate Cyient Semiconductor fundraise to establish independent value and fund the path to breakeven — while Jul 2026 drew the boundary by ruling out a DLM demerger for now.

points.point: First articulation of the separation: Cyient already has end-to-end turnkey ASIC capability (design, fabricate, test, prototype, sell) and wants a dedicated business for it, explicitly modelled on the Cyient DLM value unlock.

points.quote: Coming to the highlights for this quarter , It is my pleasure to announce that the Semiconductor business carve out process is completed as planned.

points.point: Asked to reconcile a buyback with a simultaneous fundraise, Krishna Bodanapu separated the two: the buyback sits at Cyient (given its capital requirements and the share price level), while the fundraise sits at Cyient Semiconductor to establish an independent value and fund it to breakeven.
points.quote: So the buyback is for Cyient. The fundraise is for Cyient Semiconductor.

points.point: The explicit purpose of raising outside capital in the carved-out entity is price discovery on a value management believes is trapped — a modest raise sized to reach breakeven, timed toward the end of a period the transcript cuts off.
points.quote: Now for Cyient Semiconductor, I think we want to establish an independent value because we believe there is a huge value unlock in Cyient Semiconductor.

points.point: Rajas Joshi of ChrysCapital pushed for a clean DLM demerger as a shareholder value unlock for the main Cyient entity — investor pressure for a second separation.

verdict.rationale: These texts do not describe a separation, demerger or spin-off at all — they describe the opposite, a buy-in and full consolidation, so no separation rationale can be reconstructed from them. The only transaction explained is Eris Lifesciences' acquisition of the remaining 30% of Swiss Parenterals Limited (parenterals, incorporated 4 February 1997, presence in ~80+ countries) from Mr. Naishadh Shah, a Director of Swiss, taking Eris from 70% to 100% so that Swiss becomes a wholly owned subsidiary. The stated objects are 'fully consolidating its position, enhancing operational synergy, and strengthening its long-term strategic presence', with expected benefits of complete managerial control, full financial consolidation, improved cost efficiencies, streamlined governance and enhanced shareholder value. Consideration is INR 423.30 crore, discharged not in cash but by a preferential issue of up to 23,06,372 equity shares of face value Re. 1 at INR 1,835.35 each (premium INR 1,834.35), taking Mr. Shah from nil to 1.69% on a fully diluted basis, priced per Chapter V of the SEBI ICDR Regulations and a valuation report of 24 November 2025 by Rashmi Shah, Independent Registered Valuer (IBBI/RV/06/2018/10240). It is disclosed as a related party transaction (a transaction with a related party of a subsidiary under Regulation 2(zc) of SEBI LODR), stated to be at arm's length, with no promoter/promoter group/group company interest, no governmental or regulatory approvals required, and completion expected before 31 March 2026. The scale cited for Swiss is group-level turnover of INR 220.80 crore (FY2022-23), INR 282.97 crore (FY2023-24) and INR 351.11 crore (FY2024-25). No business is being carved out, no resulting entity is named, no demerger scheme or rationale clause is present, and no party (investor, lender or partner) is identified as having asked for anything.
verdict.evolution: No earnings call passages were supplied — the 'CALL PASSAGES' section is empty, so there is no call-by-call history to trace. The documentary trail runs only across two Regulation 30 intimations: the Board meeting of 24 November 2025 (2:45 PM to 5:30 PM) approving the 30% Swiss acquisition, the share-swap consideration and a postal ballot with a 21 November 2025 cut-off date; and the intimation of 16 January 2026 recording that shareholders approved by postal ballot on 24 December 2025 and that the Board's Executive Committee approved the allotment of the 23,06,372 shares that day. The plan therefore did not change over time in these texts — it moved from board approval to shareholder approval to allotment without alteration, and the filing explicitly records 'None' against any cancellation or termination of the issuance proposal.

points.point: The transaction is a consolidation, not a separation: Eris proposes to move from its existing 70% holding to 100% ownership of Swiss Parenterals, the stated purpose being consolidation of position, operational synergy and long-term strategic presence.

verdict.rationale: The texts provided do not support a separation narrative: the CALL PASSAGES section was supplied empty (no earnings-call text at all), and the filing excerpt is a Scheme of Amalgamation, i.e. a combination rather than a separation, demerger or spin-off. In it, two wholly-owned subsidiaries of the listed parent are being merged into their holding company and dissolved: Dealskart Online Services Private Limited (incorporated 8 September 2011, CIN U74140DL2011PTC224819, PAN AADCD9571D), which provides operations and maintenance (O&M) services to the parent's omni-channel stores PAN India, and Lenskart Eyetech Private Limited (incorporated 2 July 2015, CIN U74110DL2015PTC282327, PAN AACCL8854C), which operates training centres for retail staff. The Transferee Company is Lenskart Solutions Limited (originally incorporated 19 May 2008 as Valyoo Technologies Private Limited, renamed on conversion to a public company on 16 June 2025, CIN L33100DL2008PLC178355), a listed entity on NSE and BSE, engaged in designing, manufacturing, branding and retailing eyewear, and the holding company of both transferors. The only stated motive visible in the excerpt is tax and legal form: the scheme is drawn to comply with the conditions for an 'amalgamation' under Section 2(6) of the Income Tax Act, 2025 and other applicable provisions. The structural plumbing is set out as Parts A–E, covering introduction and rationale, share capital, amalgamation of the transferors into the transferee, consideration, accounting treatment and dissolution of the transferors, and general terms. Beyond this, the substantive 'Purpose and Rationale' clauses of Part A are cut off by the truncation, so no synergy, margin, capital, focus, valuation, investor, lender or partner rationale is stated anywhere in the supplied material. No businesses are identified as being separated, and no numbers, demands from investors/lenders/partners, or management commentary of any kind appear in these texts.
verdict.evolution: No evolution can be traced: the prompt's CALL PASSAGES block contains no passages, so there are no call labels or call dates in evidence, and nothing can be attributed to management across three years of calls. The only dated markers in the supplied text are corporate-history dates in the filing — incorporation on 19 May 2008 as Valyoo Technologies Private Limited, the subsidiaries' incorporations on 8 September 2011 and 2 July 2015, and conversion to a public limited company renamed Lenskart Solutions Limited on 16 June 2025. Within the filing itself the proposal appears only in its final form, as an amalgamation of the two wholly-owned subsidiaries into the listed parent.

verdict.hidden_value: Broadway is immaterial to the parent: turnover ₹9.63 cr (0.07%), total income ₹9.90 cr (0.07%), net worth ₹38.99 cr (0.24%), yet sold for ₹49.00 cr — above book net worth, bringing cash to the parent.

verdict.quote: As part of the Company’s strategy to divest it’s non-core assets, the Board of Directors of the Company at its meeting held today i.e. July 11, 2026, has approved the divestment of 100% stake in Broadway, to AKRK Projects LLP and Partners and authorised for execution of Share Purchase Agreement.

verdict.rationale: On these texts alone, there is no demerger or spin-off of a pharmaceutical business being explained — the only 'separation' documented is a non-core asset exit: at its July 11, 2026 board meeting Mankind approved divesting 100% of Broadway Hospitality Services Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary, to AKRK Projects LLP and Partners for ₹49.00 crore (subject to closing adjustment), to be completed within 90 days, with the stated reason being 'the Company's strategy to divest it's non-core assets'. The size disclosures make the logic plain: Broadway contributed FY26 revenue of ₹9.63 crore (0.07% of the company), total income ₹9.90 crore (0.07%) and net worth ₹38.99 crore (0.24%) — a hospitality business immaterial to a pharma company, sold to a non-promoter, non-related party. The same board approved the opposite leg of the reshaping: a new Netherlands wholly owned subsidiary as an SPV to hold R&D assets and do business development in niche therapies, through joint ventures or strategic interests, with investment of up to EUR 5 million in tranches — i.e. cash out of non-core hospitality, capital into focused R&D/in-licensing. A third, earlier step in the same clean-up was the April 13, 2026 approval to wind up Mankind Pharma Lanka (Private) Limited, a non-operating, non-material Sri Lankan WOS, because 'changed regulatory requirements' made the anticipated business objectives no longer viable. The earnings calls supply the cultural/structural argument rather than any scheme rationale: on Jan 2025 management cited the OTC business as precedent, where they corrected practices by 'hiving off', cutting the number of distributors and bringing in outside talent so one leader no longer ran OTC and pharma together, after which growth improved, and said 80–90% of the analogous changes in the Mankind Pharma Delhi division were complete with one quarter to go. The Nov 2024 call frames the productivity problem behind that focus push: the chronic-focused specialty division has productivity below the company average, newer specialty divisions (MD/DM/KOL-facing, launched in the last 3–4 years) run at about ₹3 lakh PCPM against ₹8–10 lakh in the legacy multi-specialty divisions carrying brands like Telmikind and Amlokind (₹400–500 crore each), and acute versus chronic cannot be carved out because divisions were launched as multi-specialty; chronic was ~28% of the mix five years ago. On BSV, management argued the acquired business is 'a totally different ball game' — super-specialty, critical care, gynec, IVF — with only 5–10% overlap, the exception being the TTK portfolio's 3–4 branded-prescription divisions that move to the Delhi side for optimisation; BSV's PCPM averaged 6.5 last year, but excluding TTK (under 3) the rest is upwards of ₹8 lakh.
verdict.evolution: Nov 05, 2024: the groundwork is diagnostic rather than structural — low-productivity chronic/specialty divisions (~₹3 lakh PCPM vs ₹8–10 lakh legacy), an admission that acute and chronic cannot be carved out of multi-specialty divisions, and BSV described as near-zero overlap except the TTK divisions to be re-homed to Delhi. Jan 2025: the method is named, with OTC as the template — 'hiving off', separate leadership for OTC versus pharma, distributor rationalisation and outside hires — and management says 80–90% of the same changes in the Delhi division are done, one quarter remaining. Then a gap in the supplied record until April 13, 2026, when the board winds up the dormant Sri Lanka WOS, and July 11, 2026, when it converts the 'focus' theme into balance-sheet action: sell Broadway for ₹49 crore as non-core, and seed a Netherlands R&D/niche-therapy SPV with up to EUR 5 million. No call passage here ever discusses the Broadway sale, the Netherlands SPV, or any demerger of a listed business.

points.point: The productivity gap was quantified: newer specialty divisions sit around ₹3 lakh PCPM, versus ₹8–10 lakh in the multi-specialty divisions carrying ₹400–500 crore brands like Telmikind and Amlokind.

points.point: Chronic mix had been built up from a low base — about 28% of sales five years earlier — which is why newer chronic/specialty divisions are still immature on productivity.
points.quote: But to add to Prakash point, around 5 years ago, our chronic contribution was ~28%.

points.point: BSV is positioned as a structurally separate super-specialty business (critical care, gynec, IVF) with almost no field overlap with base Mankind — only 5–10%.
points.quote: BSV is a totally different ball game .

points.point: The one integration/reorganisation item is the TTK portfolio: 3–4 branded prescription divisions move to the Delhi side, where optimisation will take place; overlap is otherwise 5–10%.
points.quote: We see 5 - 10% overlapping that's all, nothing more.

points.point: TTK is the drag on acquired productivity: BSV's average PCPM was 6.5 last year, but excluding TTK (under 3) the remainder is upwards of ₹8 lakh.

points.point: Management offered the OTC business as the explicit precedent for separation: hiving off, rationalising distributors, bringing in different talent, and ending a mixed culture where one leader ran both OTC and pharma — after which growth improved.
